chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amari ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the beggar who begs by his palm, would his testimony be accepted? So he said: My father (peace be upon him) did not accept his testimony when he begs by his palm.

key_terms.يَسْأَلُ فِي كَفِّهِ: begs by his palm (holding out hand for alms)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a beggar accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights a specific juristic criterion for witness credibility (*shahada*), where Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) rejects the testimony of one who begs with an open palm, linking financial independence to social dignity and reliability. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the moral character (*'adl*) of witnesses, suggesting that habitual reliance on charity may indicate a lack of self-sufficiency or dignity required for legal testimony. The attribution to the Imam's father, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS), underscores the continuity of this legal principle within the Ahl al-Bayt's jurisprudential tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amaraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the beggar who begs by his palm, would his testimony be accepted?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His testimony is not acceptable when he begs by his palm’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a beggar man who extends his hand for begging, if his testimony is acceptable.
He (the Imam) said, ‘My father would not accept his testimony if he extended his hand for begging.’”
